newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to cut spending, current account deficit.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to cut spending, current account deficit.

text.p: Pakistan will curtail its public spending in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) by one percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) to help lower the fiscal deficit to five percent of GDP, an official said on Tuesday.

"In the next budget public expenditure will be curtailed by another one percent on top of a two percent cut already achieved this year," Hafeez Pasha, Deputy Chairman of the state's Planning Commission, told a business conference in Karachi.
Pasha did not give further details.
He said the fiscal deficit by the end of fiscal 1996/97 would be between six to 6.5 percent of the GDP, compared to last years deficit of 6.3 percent.

"The fiscal deficit could have further worsened but the government during the past few months succeeded in bring down the public expenditure to 21 percent of the GDP from 23 percent - a feat never achieved before," he added.
